saints.name: The Martyrs of September
saints.title: Martyrs of the French Revolution
saints.shortBlurb: The bishops, priests, and religious slaughtered in the Paris prisons for refusing the revolutionary oath against the Church…
biography: During the Terror of the French Revolution, on 2 and 3 September 1792, mobs broke into the improvised prisons of Paris — above all the Carmelite convent (the Carmes) — and massacred clergy and religious who had refused to swear the schismatic Civil Constitution of the Clergy. Among them was Jean-Marie du Lau, Archbishop of Arles, together with the brothers François and Pierre de La Rochefoucauld, bishops of Beauvais and of Saintes.

One hundred and ninety-one of these victims, who met death rather than repudiate their communion with the Pope, were beatified by Pope Pius XI in 1926. Their witness stands with that of the many other priests and religious put to death across France in those years.
saints.knownFor: Dying rather than swear the oath that would have severed them from the Church.

sources.text: Vatican, Beatification of the Martyrs of Paris of September 1792 (vatican.va)
